en: Sorry, someone is sitting here.
context: Politely saying a seat is taken.
explain: Is sitting shows the person is there right now.

en: Which one do you like more?
context: Asking a friend to choose between two things.
explain: Which is used when there are limited choices.

en: I like the blue one.
explain: One replaces a noun so you do not need to repeat it.

en: Do you know how to cook?
explain: Know how to is used for a skill or ability.

en: Not really, but I can make tea.
explain: Not really is a soft no. Can talks about ability.

en: Can I use your phone for a minute?
tamil: ஒரு நிமிஷம் உங்க போனை யூஸ் பண்ணலாமா?
explain: Can I is used to ask for permission. For a minute shows it is short.

en: Of course, here you go.
context: Giving something to a person who asked.
explain: Here you go is what we say when we hand something over.

en: What are your plans for Sunday?
context: Making weekend plans with a friend.
explain: Plans for plus a day is a natural way to ask about the future.

en: I am going to visit my grandparents.
tamil: நான் என் தாத்தா பாட்டியைப் பார்க்கப் போறேன்.
explain: Am going to shows a plan you already decided.

en: Why did you not pick up my call yesterday?
context: Asking a friend with some worry.
explain: Did you not is the full form of didn't you. Pick up means to answer a call.

en: My phone battery was dead.
explain: Dead here means fully empty. Was is the past form for a single thing.

en: Where did you buy this bag?
context: Asking about a nice thing someone has.
explain: Did is used for past questions and buy stays in the base form.

alt.en: Where did you get that bag from?

en: I got it from the market near my house.
tamil: என் வீட்டுப் பக்கத்துல இருக்கிற மார்க்கெட்டுல வாங்கினேன்.
explain: Got it from is a natural way to say where you bought something.

en: What is the price of this shirt?
context: Asking the price in a shop.
explain: The price of is a clear way to ask the cost of something.

en: It costs only two hundred rupees.
explain: Costs has s because it is for one thing. Only shows it is not much.

en: Have you completed your assignment?
explain: Have you completed asks if the work is done by now.

en: No, I haven't started yet.
explain: Haven't is short for have not. Yet is used in negative sentences and questions.

en: Could you please speak a little slowly?
tamil: கொஞ்சம் மெதுவா பேச முடியுமா, தயவு செய்து?
context: Politely asking someone who speaks fast.
explain: Could is more polite than can. A little slowly softens the request.

alt.en: Please speak slowly, I did not understand.

en: Sure, is this speed okay for you?
tamil: சரி, இந்த வேகம் உனக்கு ஓகே வா?
context: Replying kindly to a speed request.
explain: A short question after sure checks that the other person is comfortable.

en: Can you tell me the way to the station?
explain: Tell me the way is a common way to ask for directions.
